statement: Report estimates 1.5°C warming since the 1950s and rainfall decline from 85 mm (1950) to 63 mm (2020); June 2020-November 2022 drought affected up to one-third of people and worsened food insecurity.
compact_statement: Report estimates 1.5°C warming since the 1950s and rainfall decline from 85 mm (1950) to 63 mm (2020); June 2020-November 2022 drought affected up to one-third of people and worsened food insecurity.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4, section A, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 65), climate trends and drought effects.

uncertainty: Up-to-one-third estimate; no regional breakdown here.

statement: The report states that floods occur nearly once every two years, have destroyed villages and livestock, and on several occasions disrupted at least 10,000 livelihoods and caused about 10 deaths.
compact_statement: The report states that floods occur nearly once every two years, have destroyed villages and livestock, and on several occasions disrupted at least 10,000 livelihoods and caused about 10 deaths.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4, section A, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 65), flood impacts.

uncertainty: The cited passage does not identify locations or dates for the individual flood events.

statement: World Bank modeling in the report estimates climate-related GDP losses of 9.3% by 2050 under its dry/pessimistic scenario without adaptation, compared with 5.7% with partial adaptation.
compact_statement: World Bank modeling in the report estimates climate-related GDP losses of 9.3% by 2050 under its dry/pessimistic scenario without adaptation, compared with 5.7% with partial adaptation.
scenario: Dry/pessimistic climate scenario; no adaptation compared with selected partial adaptation measures.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4, printed pp. 26-27 and 60 (PDF pp. 33-34, 67), climate macroeconomic scenario summary and adaptation comparison.

uncertainty: Model result aggregates selected impact channels; it is not an observed GDP loss.

statement: The G5 CCDR projects that under medium growth and its dry/pessimistic climate scenario without adaptation, Mauritania’s poverty rate in 2050 would be 0.2 percentage points above the no-climate baseline.
compact_statement: The G5 CCDR projects that under medium growth and its dry/pessimistic climate scenario without adaptation, Mauritania’s poverty rate in 2050 would be 0.2 percentage points above the no-climate baseline.
scenario: Medium-growth baseline with dry/pessimistic climate scenario; no adaptation.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.1.6, printed p. 73 (PDF p. 73), modeled poverty impact under climate scenarios.

uncertainty: The reported change is relative to the no-climate baseline and uses 2017 household-survey data in a macro-microsimulation.

statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: The study identifies poverty, food insecurity, gender inequality, limited services and youth employment as peacebuilding pressures.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: The study identifies poverty, food insecurity, gender inequality, limited services and youth employment as peacebuilding pressures.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, p. 1, opening paragraph and climate-peace pathways introduction.

uncertainty: General structural vulnerability/peacebuilding diagnosis, not itself a complete climate-conflict mechanism.

statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: Outside Mbera, the study reports host-refugee grazing competition and possible water-access discord across refugee arrival cohorts.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: Outside Mbera, the study reports host-refugee grazing competition and possible water-access discord across refugee arrival cohorts.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, p. 2, first two climate-peace pathways.

uncertainty: Executive-summary qualitative pathway, partly prospective; outside Mbera is the geographic limit, not an incident map or violence rate.

statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: The study links changing rainfall and altered traditional transhumance to farmer-herder and inter-herder conflict.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: The study links changing rainfall and altered traditional transhumance to farmer-herder and inter-herder conflict.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, p. 2, farmer-herder and inter-herder pathway.

uncertainty: Source-stated transhumance/resource-competition pathway, not isolated climate causality or incident-level attribution.

statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: Women and youth face marginalization and security risks amid livelihood disruption and displacement.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: Women and youth face marginalization and security risks amid livelihood disruption and displacement.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, p. 2, final pathway on gender, youth and security risk.

uncertainty: The summary does not quantify the change in security risk.

statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: The study identifies communal committees and government disaster-risk-reduction and climate-policy efforts as existing coping capacities.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: The study identifies communal committees and government disaster-risk-reduction and climate-policy efforts as existing coping capacities.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, p. 1, methodology and coping-capacity description.

statement: Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF rates child climate exposure and vulnerability high or very high in 11 wilayas; six highest-risk are Hodh El Chargui, Gorgol, Hodh El Gharbi, Guidimakha, Tagant and Assaba; poorest, least-served children face greatest risks.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF rates child climate exposure and vulnerability high or very high in 11 wilayas; six highest-risk are Hodh El Chargui, Gorgol, Hodh El Gharbi, Guidimakha, Tagant and Assaba; poorest, least-served children face greatest risks.
affected_groups: children with limited access to basic services

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 15 (PDF p. 14), executive-summary findings; pp. 29-30 (PDF pp. 28-29), child-risk maps.

uncertainty: Composite child climate-risk score; it is not an FCV classification.

statement: Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF estimates about half of Hodh El Chargui communities face severe or high drought risk.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF estimates about half of Hodh El Chargui communities face severe or high drought risk.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 34 (PDF p. 33), drought and water-scarcity trends.

uncertainty: The report does not name communities or provide a current update.

statement: Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF links drought and water scarcity to rainfed-crop and livestock losses, child poverty and malnutrition, rural out-migration, and possible abuse or exploitation when families send children to cities.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF links drought and water scarcity to rainfed-crop and livestock losses, child poverty and malnutrition, rural out-migration, and possible abuse or exploitation when families send children to cities.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 35-36 (PDF pp. 34-35), effects of water scarcity and drought on children.

uncertainty: Risk narrative linking livelihood disruption and possible child exploitation, not measured local protection incidence.

statement: Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF reports 2022 flood damage in Tagant, Assaba and Hodh El Gharbi; it warns flood displacement can expose children to violence, exploitation and trafficking.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF reports 2022 flood damage in Tagant, Assaba and Hodh El Gharbi; it warns flood displacement can expose children to violence, exploitation and trafficking.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 38-39 (PDF pp. 37-38), 2022 flood impacts and child protection/service disruption.

uncertainty: Historical 2022 flood damage and prospective protection risks; inconsistent housing-loss figures omitted.

statement: Source dated 2024-08-02 reports: As of 30 June 2024, Mbera hosted 108,059 registered refugees; women and children were 83% of camp registrants.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-08-02 reports: As of 30 June 2024, Mbera hosted 108,059 registered refugees; women and children were 83% of camp registrants.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 1, overall country situation and Mbera Camp figures; as-of date shown in report header.

uncertainty: Historical registration snapshot; it should not be read as a 2026 population estimate.

statement: Source dated 2024-08-02 reports: UNHCR reports Mali's humanitarian-security crisis drove arrivals into Hodh Chargui, with camp saturation sending many to neighboring villages and straining services and natural resources in a poor, climate-shock-vulnerable region.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-08-02 reports: UNHCR reports Mali's humanitarian-security crisis drove arrivals into Hodh Chargui, with camp saturation sending many to neighboring villages and straining services and natural resources in a poor, climate-shock-vulnerable region.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 1, overall situation; PDF p. 2, out-of-camp response and Population Flow Monitoring.

uncertainty: Historical conflict-driven arrivals and resource/service pressure; no measured resulting violence or climate cause of refugee status.

statement: Source dated 2024-08-02 reports: UNHCR reports monthly arrival monitoring in over 60 villages and an area-based response with partners and local authorities for refugees and host communities.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-08-02 reports: UNHCR reports monthly arrival monitoring in over 60 villages and an area-based response with partners and local authorities for refugees and host communities.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2, out-of-camp response paragraphs and map showing host communes.

uncertainty: The report states response objectives and monitoring, not effectiveness.

statement: Source dated 2025-09-09 reports: By end-August 2025, rainfall deficits persisted in Hodh Ech Chargui and Hodh El Gharbi; dry spells and floods caused localized crop losses.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-09-09 reports: By end-August 2025, rainfall deficits persisted in Hodh Ech Chargui and Hodh El Gharbi; dry spells and floods caused localized crop losses.

source_refs.locator: Country brief, reference date 9 September 2025, rainfall and crop conditions paragraphs.

uncertainty: Seasonal report; local crop-loss locations are not specified.

statement: Source dated 2025-09-09 reports: For June-August 2025, FAO reports about 44,000 refugees in Hodh Ech Chargui faced acute food insecurity, including over 6,000 in Phase 4; 17% of resident Mauritanians needed aid.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-09-09 reports: For June-August 2025, FAO reports about 44,000 refugees in Hodh Ech Chargui faced acute food insecurity, including over 6,000 in Phase 4; 17% of resident Mauritanians needed aid.

source_refs.locator: Country brief, reference date 9 September 2025, Hodh Ech Chargui food-security section.

uncertainty: June–August 2025 food-security estimates, not current 2026 values; refugee and resident denominators differ.

statement: Source dated 2025-09-09 reports: FAO reports government support for irrigation infrastructure and inputs; rainfed support includes dam and dike work, seeds and improved equipment access.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-09-09 reports: FAO reports government support for irrigation infrastructure and inputs; rainfed support includes dam and dike work, seeds and improved equipment access.

source_refs.locator: Country brief, reference date 9 September 2025, 2025 crop-support paragraphs.

uncertainty: FAO describes support measures but does not evaluate their effectiveness.
